entries.reason: Core owns the message buffer, so caller bytes are copied into native storage before the handle is returned.
Bytes is the explicit lifetime-independent snapshot API; the copy is required after the native message may close.
Message submit preserves the caller handle when Core rejects a send, so the native submit frame is copied before submission.
Each received native part needs a Go owner while zlink_msg_adopt transfers the Core buffer without a payload copy.
Core writes topic metadata into caller-provided storage; the result objects retain one reusable buffer instead of allocating 64 KiB on every receive.
A builder supplied with []byte must materialize Core-owned messages before Submit returns.
Core writes option values into caller-provided scratch storage; returned strings and message values acquire Go ownership at the public boundary.
One dispatcher worker per callback registration preserves callback ordering and gives socket close an explicit completion owner.
One plain mutex per handle keeps a multipart record contiguous and keeps close from racing an in-flight native submit. It is not a queue or a worker: the HWM wait itself belongs to Core.
The package must link and load the runtime shipped beside the module, including in a clean consumer without repository paths.
